name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) student scholarship — umbrella rules
amount_detail: Unit contribution of EUR 1,400/month x DS (duration of the Master in months). Programme Guide formula quoted verbatim: "1 400 Euros/month x DS". For a 24-month EMJM that is EUR 33,600 total; 18 months = EUR 25,200; 12 months = EUR 16,800. NOTE — under the post-2021 EMJM design this single monthly unit REPLACED the old EMJMD three-part split (participation costs / travel+installation / subsistence). The Programme Guide states the amount "shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs" as one lump. There is NO separately published Partner-Country uplift in the 2021+ EMJM rules — the EUR 1,400/month is the same regardless of nationality. Individual consortia may still publish their own internal breakdown (e.g. EUR 1,275/month subsistence + separate travel/installation), which is a consortium presentation choice, not an EC rule.
covers: No tuition/participation fees for scholarship holders ("projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders"); no application fee; plus EUR 1,400/month covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence.
eligibility_verbatim: "EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world. However, consortia should ensure geographical balance – i.e. no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality." Students must be "enrolled at Master level who have obtained a first higher education degree or demonstrate a recognised equivalent level of learning."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: No nationality exclusion found. The only nationality-linked constraint quoted in the Programme Guide is the geographical-balance cap: "no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality." (Tunisia is not a high-volume EMJM nationality, so this cap is unlikely to bind.)
deadline_2027_intake: Set per consortium, not centrally. EMJM calls for an autumn intake typically close between October and February of the PRECEDING academic year — i.e. for a September 2027 start, expect deadlines roughly Oct 2026 – Feb 2027. NOT FOUND as a central date; must be checked per programme.
notes: CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE WORKING ASSUMPTION: the belief that Partner-Country status INCREASES the EMJM award is true of the OLD Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees (EMJMD, 2014-2020 calls), where participation-cost caps were EUR 9,000/yr for Programme Country vs EUR 25,000/yr for Partner Country students and travel/installation was EUR 1,000 vs EUR 3,000. Under the current EMJM design (2021+ calls, which is what a Sept 2027 intake will be) the grant is a flat EUR 1,400/month for everyone. Tunisian status is therefore neutral on the money, not favourable — but it is fully eligible. Second point: Tunisia is a "third country not associated to the Programme" (Region 3, South-Mediterranean). Being in that category is what makes a Tunisian applicant a normal, welcome EMJM candidate rather than one competing inside an EU quota. Third point: a Tunisian applicant with NO prior EU residency is exactly the profile EMJM targets; the only residency-linked rule some consortia apply is a mobility rule (you cannot do your mobility in the country where you obtained your first degree) — irrelevant here.

funder: European Commission / EACEA (Erasmus+ EMJM) — FULL SCHOLARSHIP SUSPENDED; coordinated by Dublin City University
amount_detail: NO FULL ERASMUS MUNDUS SCHOLARSHIP for the 2026/2028 intake. What is offered instead: "up to 24 Partial Fee Waivers and 8 EMILDAI Merit Scholarships." Partial Fee Waiver = second-year tuition only (student pays a EUR 500 deposit and full year-one fees, then year two is exempt). EMILDAI Merit Scholarship = "EUR 2000 payment per year for each year of the programme" (EUR 4,000 total), student still pays the EUR 500 deposit and regular fees.
covers: At best a partial fee reduction or EUR 4,000 cash. No living stipend, no full tuition waiver.
eligibility_verbatim: "Full Erasmus Mundus Scholarship will not be available" for this cohort, with a stated hope to restore it if future funding permits. Track-based nationality rules apply to the two instruments: the Partial Fee Waiver excludes "Non-EU students in Track C and EU students in Track D"; the EMILDAI Merit Scholarship is "Eligible only for: Non-EU students in Track C and EU students in Track D".
exclusion_clause_verbatim: "Full Erasmus Mundus Scholarship will not be available." Plus the track rule: "Ineligible tracks: Non-EU students in Track C and EU students in Track D" (for the Partial Fee Waiver). A Tunisian citizen is a non-EU student, so which instrument they can claim depends entirely on which track they enter: Track C => Merit Scholarship (EUR 2,000/yr) only; any other track => Partial Fee Waiver route. "Students who previously received an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship cannot apply for another EMJM scholarship."
deadline_2027_intake: PROBABLY NO SEPTEMBER-2027 INTAKE. EMILDAI runs biennial cohorts — the current one is labelled "2026/2028", entering September 2026, with round 1 (partially funded) opening 10 November 2025 and round 2 (self-funded only) opening 22 March 2026. On that cycle the next entry point is September 2028, not September 2027. NOT CONFIRMED by an explicit statement; a human should verify with the consortium.
notes: RUCT 4318252, active. Consortium: Dublin City University (Ireland, COORDINATOR), Avignon Universite (France), Universidad de Leon (Spain), Universita di Pisa (Italy), plus Erasmus University Rotterdam and Fundacao Getulio Vargas Rio joining from the 2026/2028 edition. Applications are made through DCU (https://dcuie2.elluciancrmrecruit.com/Apply/Account/Login), not Leon. RANK LOW: the full EMJM money is gone for the current cohort, the likely next entry is 2028 not 2027, and the subject (law + AI) is only tangentially in the nine fields. Tuition amounts and language of instruction NOT FOUND on the site.

name: MIR — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Marine and Maritime Intelligent Robotics
funder: European Commission / EACEA (Erasmus+ EMJM); coordinated by Universite de Toulon
amount_detail: "An average of 22 Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available per year for students of excellence." Amount per scholarship NOT PUBLISHED on the fees page — it says only that EMJMD scholarships cover the participation costs. Participation fees the scholarship would cover: "Program Country students (EU/EEA): EUR 4,500 per year"; "Partner Country students (non-EU): EUR 9,000 per year" — so for a Tunisian the fee waiver alone is worth EUR 18,000 over two years.
covers: Participation costs ("Enrollment and tuition costs at local universities", insurance cover, symposium participation, induction activities, conference travel for published research). Monthly subsistence amount NOT FOUND on the site.
eligibility_verbatim: "Hold at the beginning of the programme/time of registering to the programme (September) a first university degree after at least three years of university studies totaling 180 ECTS, of which at least 30 ECTS are in mathematics-related subjects." "Proficient in one programming language." "Proven B2 minimum CEFR level English proficiency." On scholarships: for 2025/2026 "Scholarships are unavailable for the upcoming academic year." Historical scholarship criteria are described as including "nationality restrictions, the 12-months rule for partner country students, and limits on same-nationality recipients."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: "Scholarships are unavailable for the upcoming academic year" (2025/2026). Also, this programme applies an EXPLICIT nationality-based FEE PENALTY: "Program Country students (EU/EEA): EUR 4,500 per year" vs "Partner Country students (non-EU): EUR 9,000 per year" — double. And self-financed students were "previously limited to study tracks in Spain or Portugal (not Norway) due to cost-of-living concerns, though this policy changes for the 2025/2027 cohort."
deadline_2027_intake: NOT FOUND. The site news mentions a "self-financed students recruitment campaign opening on May 8, 2025" for "the 2025/2026 academic year, starting in September 2025". No 2027 calendar published, and no confirmation that EM scholarships return.
notes: RUCT 4317521 (Master Universitario Erasmus Mundus en Robotica Inteligente Marina y Maritima). Consortium: Universite de Toulon (France, COORDINATOR), Universitat Jaume I (Spain), NTNU (Norway), Instituto Superior Tecnico Universidade de Lisboa (Portugal); "over 25 international research establishments" and "over 30 industry partners" associated. THIS RECORD IS THE CLEAREST EVIDENCE IN THE BLOCK THAT PARTNER-COUNTRY STATUS CUTS AGAINST THE CANDIDATE ON FEES: a Tunisian self-funder pays exactly twice what an EU student pays. The "12-months rule" the site mentions is the legacy EMJMD rule under which a Partner Country applicant qualified for the larger award only if they had not resided or carried out their main activity in a Programme Country for more than 12 months in the preceding 5 years — a candidate with NO prior EU residency satisfies it, which is the one place Partner Country status historically helped. PATH FIT POOR: marine robotics, AA only, no audio content.
